question: When should an integration use SEP-6, SEP-24, or SEP-31 for fiat on/off-ramp and cross-border flows?

golden.answer: As of 2026-11-02, SEP-6, SEP-24, and SEP-31 are Active. Use SEP-24 for an anchor-hosted interactive deposit/withdrawal UI; use SEP-6 for programmatic deposit/withdrawal—the legacy interactive SEP-6 flow is deprecated in favor of SEP-24, not the whole SEP. For SEP-31, a Sending Anchor calls a Receiving Anchor under an established bilateral or commercial relationship for cross-border payout. Discover them through SEP-1 keys TRANSFER_SERVER, TRANSFER_SERVER_SEP0024, and DIRECT_PAYMENT_SERVER respectively. Add SEP-38 when quotes or rates are part of the corridor.
keyFacts: Maps SEP-24 to anchor-hosted interactive deposit/withdrawal; SEP-6 to programmatic API.
Keeps SEP-6 Active with only its legacy interactive flow deprecated in favor of SEP-24.
Uses SEP-31 for Sending→Receiving Anchor calls with established bilateral/commercial ties.
Gives a dated Active status for SEP-6, SEP-24, and SEP-31.
Maps SEP-1 keys TRANSFER_SERVER, TRANSFER_SERVER_SEP0024, and DIRECT_PAYMENT_SERVER.
avoid: SEP-31 is simply the newest replacement for both SEP-6 and SEP-24.
SEP-24 requires the wallet to collect and host the anchor's KYC user interface.
Do NOT claim SEP-38 is an Active SEP; the protocol repo lists it as Draft.
